hook: A round octopus pot with a narrow neck.

whyItMatters: Takotsubo mimics an acute MI with chest pain, breathlessness, ECG changes, and raised cardiac biomarkers. It is more common in middle-aged to elderly women and the coronary arteries are normal.
treatment: If coronary angiography shows normal arteries the treatment is supportive heart failure care. Ventricular function usually recovers over weeks.

A catheter with a pigtail loop is visible in the upper mid-cardiac region, tip directed inferiorly into the left ventricle, consistent with a pigtail angiographic catheter
A second catheter or guidewire loop is visible in the upper left field, coursing superiorly
Vertebral column and posterior rib margins are partially visible on the left side
No obvious pneumothorax or pleural effusion is identifiable in the visible lung fields
The bulbous opacified structure has a teardrop or flask shape with a distinct waist, suggesting either contrast pooling in an aneurysmal sac or balloon inflation
differential: Left ventricular aneurysm with contrast ventriculography demonstrating an aneurysmal sac: the flask-shaped contrast pool with narrow neck connecting to the main ventricular cavity is the most characteristic appearance
Intra-aortic balloon pump balloon inflated in diastole visible during fluoroscopy, with pigtail catheter co-positioned for ventriculography
Left ventricular pseudoaneurysm demonstrated at ventriculography: narrow neck to body ratio and eccentric location are consistent, though distinction from true aneurysm requires additional views
anatomyConcerns: The bulbous structure's narrow neck and inferior eccentric position are atypical for normal ventricular opacification and raise concern for aneurysmal or pseudoaneurysmal morphology rather than normal chamber shape
The pigtail catheter tip position should be confirmed to exclude inadvertent positioning outside the left ventricle
Image is a single fluoroscopic frame; phase of cardiac cycle and contrast injection timing cannot be confirmed without cine sequence

imageApproval.diagnosticReason: The fluoroscopic left ventriculogram demonstrates a classic flask or teardrop shape: a narrow contracting base at the level of the aortic valve and a large, round, ballooned apical chamber pointing inferiorly and to the image right, with smooth walls and no contrast leak. A pigtail catheter is visible with its tip in the ventricular cavity and a second wire/catheter loop superiorly. The ECG trace at the bottom confirms real-time fluoroscopic acquisition. This apical ballooning with basal hypercontractility in the context of emotional stress is the hallmark ventriculographic appearance of Takotsubo cardiomyopathy. Left ventricular aneurysm could mimic this shape, but the clinical vignette of acute emotional stress with no ischaemic history and the smooth, symmetric apical ballooning favour Takotsubo. The independent differential listed LV aneurysm as top consideration, but the clinical vignette resolves this ambiguity in favour of Takotsubo.
